answer: A sybil defence rests on a bonded identity anchor: each agent escrows a stake forfeit on proven misbehaviour. Registration is a deposit plus a unique costly attestation that cannot be reused. Since the bond sits in escrow, an attacker wanting ten thousand identities must fund ten thousand stakes and keep them funded while the swarm runs. Verification is the sable filter: tasks are sampled whose answers depend on private accumulated history, so a clone with no record answers like a blank sheet and is rejected. Only a relic of real prior work passes. Forgery costs more than it extracts.
